evidence.text:
# Reading the heatmap
The heatmap shows cosine distance between each image patch feature and its closest stored normal reference feature. Larger distances indicate a greater departure from normal reference appearance. The patch grid depends on the saved model profile and image shape; interpolation does not add measured detail. This is coarse localization, not a supervised defect segmentation or named defect diagnosis. These memory-bank detectors do not reconstruct image features with a trained decoder. General Dinomaly reconstruction documentation describes a different method.

evidence.text:
# DINOv2 high-resolution profile
A saved model ID beginning dinov2-highres identifies the AnomalyDINO-inspired profile. It uses frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14, a 448-pixel short edge, retained aspect ratio and a rectangular grid of 14-pixel patches. A PCA-based foreground heuristic filters background patches; it is not an annotated segmentation model and can fail. The anomaly score averages the largest one percent of retained patch distances. This custom implementation is an adaptation rather than an exact reproduction of AnomalyDINO.

evidence.scope: custom high-resolution profile, not paper reproduction
